title: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the variable A/C compressor control valve. This part adjusts how hard the A/C compressor works.

causes.name: Faulty variable A/C compressor control valve
Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the variable A/C compressor control valve wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the variable A/C compressor control valve with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new variable A/C compressor control valve if it tests bad.

title: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the variable A/C compressor control valve, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part adjusts how hard the A/C compressor works.

causes.name: Faulty variable A/C compressor control valve

checks: Inspect the variable A/C compressor control valve wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the variable A/C compressor control valve with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new variable A/C compressor control valve if it tests bad.

title: Variable A/C Compressor Control Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the variable A/C compressor control valve, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part adjusts how hard the A/C compressor works.

causes.name: Faulty or shorted variable A/C compressor control valve

checks: Inspect the variable A/C compressor control valve wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the variable A/C compressor control valve with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new variable A/C compressor control valve if it tests bad.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage "D" Circuit/Open
plain: The computer feeds a steady 5-volt supply to a group of sensors, and supply "D" has dropped out or is not reaching the sensors. Several sensors can stop reading correctly at once.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: Shorted sensor on the shared 5-volt circuit (such as a throttle, pedal or pressure sensor)
Chafed or damaged wiring shorted to ground

checks: Note which other sensor codes set at the same time
Unplug sensors on that circuit one at a time and watch whether the 5-volt supply comes back
Inspect the harness for rubbing, melting or water damage
fix: Usually finding and replacing the sensor that is upsetting the supply, or repairing damaged wiring.

title: PCM/ECM/TCM Internal Temperature "B" Too High
plain: A control computer is reporting, from its second internal sensor, that it is running too hot inside.
symptoms: Reduced power, limp mode or stalling

causes.name: Shorted sensor, solenoid or actuator overloading the computer
Computer mounted near a heat source or blocked cooling
Low or overheated transmission fluid (computers mounted in the transmission)

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix any shorted part or heat problem first; otherwise replace and program the computer.

title: PCM/ECM/TCM Internal Temperature Sensor "B" Circuit
plain: A control computer has a second temperature sensor ("B") inside it to protect itself from overheating, and that sensor has a circuit problem.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Low voltage or poor power and ground at the computer
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and computer power and ground circuits
Check for software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement.

title: Torque Management System - Forced Engine Shutdown
plain: The computer shut the engine off on purpose as a safety measure because it saw the engine making power that was not requested.
symptoms: Reduced power or limp mode codes stored with it

causes.name: Faulty accelerator pedal or throttle position sensor signal
Sticking or faulty electronic throttle body
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Read all other stored codes, especially throttle and pedal codes
Inspect the throttle body and its wiring
Check for software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Repair the throttle, pedal or sensor fault that triggered the shutdown; sometimes a computer update or replacement.
drive: No, not until it's checked. The computer shut the engine off because it saw power you didn't ask for, so it no longer trusts throttle control. If it restarts, drive only to a safe spot or a very close shop, and have it towed if it shuts off again or the pedal feels wrong.
test_first: Read all stored codes, especially throttle and pedal codes, then check pedal and throttle sensor signals, the throttle body and wiring, and look for software updates before replacing the computer.

title: Sensor Power Supply "A" Circuit/Open
plain: The computer powers a group of sensors through supply "A", and that supply is missing or broken.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: Shorted sensor on the supply circuit

checks: Note which sensor codes set at the same time
Check fuses for the sensor supply
Unplug sensors on the circuit one at a time to find a short
fix: Usually replacing a shorted sensor or repairing the wiring or fuse.

title: Internal Control Module Knock Sensor Processor 1 Performance
plain: The part of the engine computer that listens to the knock sensors (processor 1) failed a self-check.
symptoms: Possible reduced power or poor fuel economy

causes.name: Shorted knock sensor or knock sensor wiring
Low voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

symptoms: Possible reduced power or poor fuel economy

causes.name: Shorted knock sensor or knock sensor wiring
Low voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)

title: Internal Control Module Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM) Error
plain: The engine computer found an error in the memory that keeps learned settings when the key is off.
symptoms: Idle or shifting may feel off until the computer relearns

causes.name: Low battery voltage or poor power or ground connections at the computer
Computer software that needs an update or reprogramming
Water damage or corrosion at the computer connector

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The glow plug for cylinder 1 is drawing more or less current than the computer expects. Glow plugs heat the cylinders so a diesel engine starts easily in cold weather.
symptoms: Rough running or white smoke right after a cold start

causes.name: High resistance from a corroded or loose glow plug connector

checks: Measure the cylinder 1 glow plug resistance and current draw
Inspect the glow plug connector for corrosion
fix: Usually a new glow plug or a connector repair.
